back: Bounded data has an end (yesterday's files); unbounded data never ends (a click stream). Batch is streaming over bounded input.
Correctness vs latency vs cost: you can tune how complete, how fast and how expensive results are, but not maximise all three.
Event time: when it happened, stamped by the producer. Processing time: when the processor sees it. The gap is skew.

front: Why do processing-time results change on replay?
back: Events land in whatever window the processor's clock was in when it read them, which differs on every run and every backlog.
Fixed size, no overlap (10:00–10:01, 10:01–10:02). Each event is in exactly one window.
Each event lands in size ÷ slide windows. 10-min size, 1-min slide = 10 updates per event and 10 open windows per key.
Groups a key's events separated by less than an inactivity gap. Variable length; late events can merge two sessions.

front: Cheap way to compute a 1-hour rolling sum per second?
back: Pre-aggregate into small tumbling buckets (1 minute) and add the last 60 per key, instead of 3,600 overlapping windows.
The system's claim that event time has reached T: no more events older than T are expected. Windows fire when it passes their end.
Largest event timestamp seen minus the bound (minus 1 ms). Bound 5 s, max seen 12:00:20 → watermark ≈ 12:00:15.

front: Why can one idle partition stall a whole Flink job?
back: An operator's watermark is the minimum over its inputs; an input with no events never advances. Fix with withIdleness().

front: Kafka Streams' equivalent of a watermark?
back: Stream time (largest timestamp seen per task); a window closes when stream time passes window end plus the grace period.
Drop it (Flink default, counted in numLateRecordsDropped), update the result (allowed lateness / grace), or divert it (side output).

front: What must a sink do if windows re-fire for late data?
back: Accept updates: upsert by a deterministic key such as campaign + window start, not append a new row.

front: Three ingredients of end-to-end exactly-once effects?
back: A replayable source, consistent snapshots of state plus input offsets, and an idempotent or transactional sink.

front: How does a Flink checkpoint stay consistent?
back: Barriers flow with the data; each operator snapshots state when the barrier arrives, so state matches the saved source offsets.

front: Latency cost of a transactional exactly-once sink?
back: Output becomes visible to read_committed consumers only when the checkpoint commits: up to one checkpoint interval late.

front: Flink vs Kafka Streams in one line?
back: Flink is a cluster engine for many sources and large state; Kafka Streams is a library inside your app, Kafka in and Kafka out.
